summary: Validated update (valid; effect: interpretation append for the recovery-authority question, rationale only), and the source check behind it confirmed the code directly: handlePrepareReply's mismatched-ballot branch is three lines - compare the reply ballot, increment lb.nacks, return - followed only by the append and the slow-quorum guard, so a rejection has no repair call and never reaches the guard. That closure is exactly what the account's resolved gap asserts, so nothing in the statement, citations or limits changed; only the re-check is recorded. This was the last source-level check I had outstanding. Final state of the run: six questions, all explained, each on controller receipts - value adoption replacing the quorum-reported command with a NOOP up to a completed contradiction of a live replica's committed value, with the defect bounded to coordinators lacking the command by an executed control run; recovery authority bounded by the recoverer's fixed ballot, the only repairs being the two IsLeader-gated restarts in the proposal-phase handlers, now source-verified together with the rejection branch; the status-guard stall that clears only on the executor's retry; the client-completion contract holding for the single-NOOP case through re-propose but not for the empty batch; the wrong-row write in handlePreAccept refuted as unreachable; and the equal-ballot empty-slice replacement decided by the reply adopted at the slow-quorum trigger position, measured over all six permutations of the three-reply set and four orders of a two-carrier/two-empty set, final because only N - SlowQuorumSize replies can follow. Eleven receipts, seven registered source materials spanning the recovery, executor and decoder paths, both facts and every behaviour entry mutually consistent in statements, conditions, dependency pointers and citations after this run's corrections, and the captured snapshot untouched throughout.
